# asciipaper engine

> A GPU renderer that turns one GLSL function into animated ASCII art: live wallpapers,
> page backgrounds, looping GIFs and stills. Native C (Wayland layer-shell, OpenGL ES) plus
> a WebGL 1 runtime that runs the same shaders and specs. Made to be driven by an agent.

## Quick start

- Build: `make` (produces `native/asciipaper-engine`).
- Live wallpaper: `./native/asciipaper-engine plasma`
- One frame: `./native/asciipaper-engine --spec wallpapers/specs/tunnel.json --lib wallpapers/lib --snapshot out.png --size 1920x1080 --seconds 6`
- Video/GIF: add `--record 30` and pipe raw BGRA frames into ffmpeg.
- Browser: `python3 -m http.server -d wallpapers 8000`, then `/run.html?spec=specs/plasma.json`;
  `/embed.html` shows a scene inside a page section.
- Tests: `make test`.

## The agent loop

1. Write a spec JSON plus a shader (`vec4 cell(vec2 uv)` returning `vec4(rgb, level)`).
2. `--snapshot try.png --seconds N` renders a deterministic frame; look at it.
3. Change the shader or the look (`charset`, `cell`, `palette`, `dither`, `shape`, `effects`,
   `interaction` in the spec; names in `wallpapers/lib/looks.json`), render again.
4. Export: `--snapshot` for a still, `--record | ffmpeg` for a clip, or hand the JSON to the
   web runtime: `asciipaper.ascii({canvas, glsl, ...})` / `asciipaper.load('wallpaper.json')`.

No network, no accounts, no cloud. `--seconds` makes renders repeatable; `--pointer X,Y`
simulates the pointer.

## Layout

- `native/` — C renderer: one layer-shell output per monitor, spec loader, cell pass, glyph
  pass, PNG/video export, pointer input.
- `wallpapers/lib/asciipaper.js` — WebGL 1 renderer (frame pacing, pointer, atlas, both
  passes), `looks.json` (shape, charset, dither, palette, effect tables), `media.glsl`,
  `legacy.js` for the four built-in interactive scenes.
- `wallpapers/specs/` — example wallpapers. `wallpapers/run.html`, `wallpapers/embed.html`.
- `tools/generate_runtime.py` — generates `native/shaders.h`, `wallpapers/lib/legacy.js` and
  the catalogs so both renderers stay identical.

## Uniforms

`u_time`, `u_aspect`, `u_grid`, `u_size`, `u_pointer`, `u_velocity`, `u_down`, `u_strength`,
`u_idle`, `u_clicks[8]`, `u_data`. GLSL ES 1.0. A shader's first line may be
`// defaults: {"speed": 1}`.
